subject: PO line-item mapping, invoice window and consolidated billing options
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@stellarhealth.com>
To: ava_chen@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO requirements and invoice cadence for Redwood deployment

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is aligned on picking Redwood for the beta. Before legal and finance can sign off, procurement needs clarity on a few billing/PO items so our AP can process invoices: 

- PO formatting: We require a 2-line PO (one line per product SKU) with a single top-level PO number. Each invoice must clearly reference the PO number and include a short description per line item. Can you confirm Redwood can emit invoices like that?
- GL/Cost center mapping: Our ERP requires a GL code or cost-center string per invoice line. Is there a standard field Redwood can populate?
- Invoice cadence: We usually prefer consolidated monthly invoices to reduce AP overhead. Is consolidated monthly billing possible even if usage varies through the month?
- Net terms: We need net60 for new vendors. Is net60 possible while the contract is still in procurement, or do you require net30 initially?
- Remittance and invoice delivery: We need invoices delivered to invoices@stellarhealth.com and a PDF copy to be uploaded to our procurement portal.

Attaching our PO template (Stellar_PO_template.xlsx) with the ERP field examples. Please loop in billing if needed.

Best,
Maya Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
Stellar Health

From: ava_chen@redwoodinference.com
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements and invoice cadence for Redwood deployment

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list and the template. Quick answers up front, then detail below:

- Yes, we can produce invoices that reference a single top-level PO and include multiple line items (2-line layout is fine).
- We support a per-line "billing_metadata" field that can carry a cost-center or GL string which we can surface on the invoice PDF and in the invoice XML export.
- Consolidated monthly invoices: supported. We can aggregate daily usage into a single monthly invoice.
- Net60: we can provision NET60 for customers with approved credit terms once procurement finishes. For initial pilots we often default to NET30 until credit checks complete, but we can request an exception to start at NET60 for your account.

Details and options:
1) PO & line items: We will ask that each SKU in your template maps to Redwood's pricing SKU (e.g., rwd-hosted-100k-tokens). If you share the final PO file we will pre-map SKUs so the resulting invoice matches your two-line requirement.

2) GL / cost center mapping: We can populate the "Account / GL" column on the PDF if you provide the exact column name to use. For automated ERP ingestion we can produce an accompanying CSV/XML file that includes the GL mapping per invoice line.

3) Consolidation cadence: By default we close invoices on the last UTC day of the calendar month and send PDFs by the 3rd business day. If you need a different cutoff (e.g., 25th of month) we can configure that as part of the billing profile.

4) Net terms / credit: To commit NET60 now we'll need a signed purchase order and your standard supplier form; our finance team will run a trade credit check which typically finishes in 3–5 business days. 

I'll loop in Ben (billing) and Neha (customer success / onboarding) to confirm the technical details and to propose one implementation path (consolidated monthly invoice + per-line GL metadata).

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@stellarhealth.com>, ava_chen@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements and invoice cadence for Redwood deployment

Hi Maya — Ben on Billing. Appreciate the template; quick confirmations and a couple of asks: 

- We can output a two-line invoice as long as the underlying usage maps to two billed SKUs. For usage-based items (token usage), we typically summarize into SKU buckets (e.g., Standard Token Tier / Overage) — if you need strict line-level matching to each API call we will need pre-defined commit bands.
- Our invoice PDF includes a "Billing metadata" column which we can populate with your cost-center/GL text. We can also include a merchant reference code that your ERP can use for reconciliation.
- Consolidating to monthly: no problem. Note that if you request a mid-month cutoff we will pro-rate the partial period and include a pro-rate line on the invoice.
- Net60: from finance's side we need either (a) a signed PO + supplier questionnaire, or (b) a prepaid commit for the first month. If procurement can turn around the supplier form quickly we can enable NET60 retroactively to the start date.

Two implementation options: 
Option A — "Monthly consolidated invoice": Redwood issues single PDF on 3rd business day; includes line items mapped to your two-line layout, plus a CSV export with GL fields.
Option B — "PO-stamped monthly statement": Redwood issues weekly invoice bundles and a month-end consolidated statement that your AP team ingests. This reduces per-invoice volume for high-transaction accounts.

Can you confirm which approach you prefer? Also attaching the SOW we normally include (Redwood_SOW_v3.pdf).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@stellarhealth.com>
To: ava_chen@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements and invoice cadence for Redwood deployment

Hi Ava / Ben — thanks for the thorough responses. Procurement preference is Option A (single consolidated monthly invoice). A few clarifying points and constraints from our ERP team: 

- The PDF must show the PO number in the header and also in each line item row (our import script validates both).
- GL code must be exactly 6 digits; if Redwood outputs a free-form string we will not be able to map. Can Redwood enforce/validate that on your export?
- We need a field called "ERP_ProjectID" passed back in the CSV for each line. Without it the import fails.
- Invoice due date must reflect NET60 based on invoice date (not statement date).
- For the pilot, Stellar will provide a single purchase order that covers the initial 2-month pilot projected consumption. If actual consumption exceeds the PO, we'll either (a) raise a top-up PO, or (b) accept an overage invoice once notified.

Attached: updated PO with GL examples. Can you provide a sample invoice (PDF + CSV) with dummy data so our ERP team can validate mapping? We need that by next Tue (10 Mar) to keep procurement timelines.

Regards,
Maya
